distinguishing_features: A physical bonded compliant elastomer/polyurethane liner is installed in the pipeline instead of a software erosion predictor or hard-facing.
The mitigation acts by low-modulus deformation and damping that increases contact time and lowers peak particle contact stress.
The liner is applied to the bottom/selected quadrants at a 10-15 mm thickness with surface preparation and curing.
Monitoring uses pressure differential and visual coating-integrity checks rather than motor-current RMS and temperature-based remaining-life integration.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to reduce particle-induced material loss at the bottom of a hydro-transport pipeline subjected to sliding bed load.
parsed.viable_reason: Bonded polyurethane/rubber liners of the stated hardness and thickness are practical, testable slurry-pipeline abrasion mitigations, and compliance can reduce contact stresses although the normal-impact model overstates the effect for sliding bed load.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Compliant rubber/polyurethane liners are a conventional slurry-erosion countermeasure, so applying one to a pipeline bottom is an obvious design alternative rather than a non-obvious mechanism.
